text:
Kayla: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands re: the new nightly soak + canary drain drills leadership mentioned. Can someone outline what the drills actually do and what PMs/CS should tell customers?

Evan: Short summary: nightly soak = run a controlled traffic profile against a small canary fleet to catch regressions; canary drain drills = simulate capacity loss by gracefully draining a subset of prewarm lanes to validate fallback paths. Both run in low-risk windows and are designed to exercise soft-failover + remap flows.

Rui: Important for CS: the drills are non-disruptive by design. We only route a tiny percentage (default 1-2%) of traffic through the canary during soak. Drain drills start with canary-only traffic, then expand to a staged subset of reserved lanes. We won't touch customer-burst buckets without opt-in.

Nora: Ops notes: schedule is nightly 02:00-03:00 UTC (UTC is best for global overlap) and a weekly extended run on Sundays. We tag runs as "nightly-soak" in the capacity dashboard. PMs can see the run history in console -> infra -> drills.

Kayla: What should PMs/CS say about SLA risk during a drill? Some folks asked if we'd ever degrade reserved customers.

Evan: TL;DR: reserved and high-SLA tenants are excluded from intrusive steps unless explicitly approved. Observable effects for non-reserved customers: tiny p99 jitter during canary soak (~20-80ms) and transient routing to quantized variants if we hit a forced drain path. We'll never intentionally violate contractual SLAs.

Rui: We added customer opt-in for extended drills. CS can enroll customers into a "canary-participation" tag if they want earlier visibility. There's also a passive telemetry export so PMs can see impact by customer_id.

Nora: Quick how-to for PMs/CS to pull the drill report: console -> infra -> drills -> select date -> export CSV. The CSV includes run_id, affected_regions, percent_canary, step_timings, and a note field with links to runbooks.

Kayla: Ops please paste a short runbook snippet we can paste into comms and the status page.

Evan: Pasteable ops snippet below (full runbook in Confluence):
```
# nightly soak + drain drill (abridged)
start_run(tag=nightly-soak, window=02:00-03:00 UTC)
set_canary_percent(1)
monitor(kpi=[p95,p99,error_rate])
if regression_detected:
  abort_canary()
  rollback_to_healthy()
  notify(#infra #cs #product)
else:
  proceed_to_drain_test(percent=5, regions=[us-west, eu-central])
  trigger_soft_failover(timeout=3m)
  validate_remap(burst_buckets)
  complete_run()
```
CSBot: Drill report template created: https://confluence.redwood/infra/drills/nightly-soak-template :white_check_mark:

Rui: Action items: Nora to pin drill schedule and export link in the all-hands notes; Evan to add explicit exclusion language for reserved SLAs to the runbook; Kayla to draft a short customer-facing blurb for CS to use.

Kayla: Thanks 9 everyone. Quick draft blurb for feedback: "We run routine, low-impact soak and drain drills to validate our routing and fallback systems. These drills help us catch regressions early and improve resiliency. Reserved customers are excluded from intrusive steps; non-reserved customers may see tiny, short-lived latency blips as we test fallbacks. If you'd like to opt-in to extended testing, contact CS." Thoughts?

Evan: Good start. Suggest adding a line about no SLA violations and link to the drill report.

Rui: 👍 also add a contact handle for opt-in requests (e.g., cs@redwood).

InfraBot: Runbook page created: https://confluence.redwood/infra/drills/nightly-soak-runbook :white_check_mark:

Kayla: Perfect. I'll finalize the blurb after Evan's edit and share with CS. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
